name: Virus-associated Trichodysplasia Spinulosa

criteria.description: Presence of folliculocentric spiny papules predominantly on the face and ears
Histological evidence of dilated hair follicles with inner root sheath cell proliferation and keratin spicules
Detection of trichodysplasia spinulosa polyomavirus (TSPyV) DNA in lesional skin by PCR or immunohistochemistry
History of immunosuppression such as organ transplantation or hematologic malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation plus histopathological confirmation and detection of TSPyV DNA
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often confirmed by combining clinical, histological, and virological findings in immunocompromised patients.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic keratin spicules arising from hair follicles
searchTerms: small spiky bumps around hair follicles

pathognomonic.notes: Hair loss localized to areas with follicular papules

pathognomonic.symptomName: Facial and ear involvement with follicular hyperkeratosis
pathognomonic.notes: Predominantly affects central face, eyebrows, and ears
searchTerms: thickened skin with rough bumps on face and ears
scaly follicle plugs on facial and ear skin
rough, bumpy skin around hair follicles on face and ears

common.notes: Mild swelling of affected facial areas
Small follicular papules resembling keratosis pilaris
searchTerms: rough skin with small bumps like chicken skin
tiny rough bumps on arms or thighs
involvement of side of the nose
redness or bumps on nose edges
puffy skin under and around eyes

occasional.notes: Occasional superinfection due to skin barrier disruption

searchTerms: mild aching or tenderness in face
soreness in facial muscles or skin

rare.notes: Very rare cases with mucosal papules

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever

laboratory: PCR detection of trichodysplasia spinulosa polyomavirus DNA in skin biopsy
Immunohistochemical staining positive for TSPyV antigens
Mild lymphopenia in peripheral blood due to immunosuppression
imaging: Not typically required; imaging generally not contributory
genetic: No known germline genetic mutations associated
other: Histopathology showing dilated hair follicles with inner root sheath cell proliferation and keratin spicules

distinguishingFeatures: Cystic lesions rather than spiny follicular papules
Histology lacks inner root sheath proliferation
Inflammatory follicular papules without viral DNA

redFlags: Rapid progression of follicular papules in immunocompromised patient
Development of extensive alopecia with facial disfigurement
Failure to respond to standard dermatological treatments
references: van der Meijden E, Janssens RW, Lauber C, et al. Discovery of a new human polyomavirus associated with trichodysplasia spinulosa in an immunocompromized patient. PLoS Pathog. 2010;6(7):e1001024.
Dalianis T, Hirsch HH. Human polyomaviruses in disease and cancer. Virology. 2013;437(2):63-72.
Kazem S, et al. Trichodysplasia spinulosa: A rare cutaneous disease in immunocompromised patients. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019;80(3):e65-e67.
